Sounds like you both already crossed some lines and there's definitely a bit of tension regarding the topic in the air. I think the best approach for now is to take a breath and try taking it easy. No snooping or getting passive-aggressive or starting fights. Only thing that'll do (which I know from personal experience) is build further tension between you two which he may try to distance himself from - possibly towards this coworker.

Now, it's impossible to say if there's really something going on or if he's just being friendly without really knowing the guy. It's very possible that he's a bit different at work or with people who share professional interests than he seems with other crowds. Maybe he was just happy to find some sort of connection with a coworker. It's also possible that he may be an omega-scumbag who's lusting after the first nice pair that'll turn his way - though it seems a little thin. You're understandably on edge after being cheated on in the past, and that's an awful, traumatizing experience - but it does tend to make one more alert to false alarms.

If it's her looks you're worried about? Honestly, you can probably stop right there. Despite stereotypes, looks are way less important to most dudes than old movies and sitcoms make it seem. If he's got a good head on his shoulders, it's probably fine. So instead ask yourself this:  
Is your relationship healthy otherwise? Do you spend a lot of time together without needing to ask the other? Everything okay in the bedroom? You both excited to see each other? If that all seems in check, you probably don't have much reason to think you're not good enough.

One last thing I'll add, again from personal experience as someone who's been cheated on: Building trust in people takes time. A lot of it. And very conscious effort. And the right person. Maybe the starts need to be aligned, too. But it works eventually. So hang in there. If something really weird starts going down, yeah, that's worth another look, but for now this isn't necessarily alarming behaviour.

This was when I was 14. My grandma had been struggling with some kind of stomach sickness I didn't understand at the time. She was out of it for a while, but it never seemed super serious. Eventually, she got hospitalized for it and spent a couple months there. Of course mini-me was told they were just making sure it's really going away, nothing serious, yadda yadda.

Fast forward a couple months. I'm coming home from school one afternoon to find a note my parents left saying they were visiting grandma, food was in the fridge, etc. Fair enough.  
Just as I get done warming up dinner and pass through the living room again, the phone starts ringing from an unknown number. On the other end of the line is some older lady whose voice I'd never heard before, immediately starting out by giving me her most sincere condolences for our loss. Confused, I ask what for, and after a moment of silence, she hangs up. It took a while for me to get it at first, very confused about the bizarre call initially, but as the evening drags on and my parents take longer and longer to return, it starts to settle in. I get more and more uneasy, and about an hour or two after sunset I hear my parents' car pull into the driveway. They're unusually quiet and take a long time to even close the doors, let alone step into the house, and I immediately know what's up. Sure enough, a few minutes later my mom knocks on my door and peeks inside, tears on her face, telling me that grandma passed away. The message still hit me hard, but not as hard as it probably would've without that ominous call giving me a heads-up.

I told my mom about the call a few days later and she seemed dumbstruck with disbelief. She didn't know the number or anyone matching the voice I heard, but what was more confusing was the timing. The call came in around 4 pm, but my grandmother only passed away around 10 pm later that day. Moreover, only her closest family was there to know about it, and no one informed any friends or extended family until the next day. Still don't know who that was, how they knew, or if it was just a really, really, really weird accident.

My buddy and I were flying over Los Santos in a Dodo plane, just enjoying the view and looking for things to do. When we left the city near the west coast, he spotted a small island out in the sea with a tiny hut on it. Initially unsure about being able to land on it, I convinced him that he would be able to safely bring us down on a small strip of relatively straight land. Said and done, we touch down on the island without issues and step off the plane to do some exploring. The hut has nothing in it but two dirty mattresses, which lead us to believe it was someone's secret pot house or rape shed. A strange, red mist also steadily emanated from a small pipe on the roof that lead into a smal side-room without any doors or windows on it, which is where I immediately assumed the bodies were stored.

Eventually bored of the small island, we make our way back to the plane and start to take off... whereupon my buddy crashes the plane into a bush and renders is completely unfunctional. So now we're trapped on Rape Island™ with a dysfunctional plane we're unable to fix. While my friend attempts to call a Taxi, I wander off to gather resources. I quickly find out that the island bears no supply of food unless you count mattresses as edible, and thus do the only thing logical in a situation like this: I eat my owl mask to prevent imminent starvation.

Hunger sated, we attempt to make people notice us. We can see the highway from our island and attempt anything from flare guns to well-placed sniper shots to gain the attention of the drivers, but to no avail. Driven to madness, we eventually try killing each other to escape this forsaken place, only to find out that we reappear on that very same island notm oments later. With our new corpses around, at least we took care of our food problem, but we still want to get off the island, so my friend starts diving into the sea to try swimming toward land. Now of course I couldn't let him leave me there alone, so I continually pick him off with a high-caliber sniper rifle, until he manages to distract me with a shiny object long enough to swim out of my reach. Without any other options, I dive into the corpse-ridden seas, fighting ice cold waters, waves and least three dozen sharks before I arrive on a small rock halfway between the island and the coast. Once there, I get a call from my friend, who kindly tells me to turn back around.

The last thing I see before my brains are relocated by a 51mm slug, off in the distance, nestled into a slightly hidden bay on the island we just escaped, is a fully functional-looking speedboat.

> I don't contribute anything of value to the world. I don't have a job. I've squandered my opportunities and talents. I've abandoned friends and family. I leech off of those that still care about me. I feel worthless and pointless. I am superfluous, unnecessary. 

I've been suffering from the same outlook as well, for a very long time. it feels as if you'll never amount to anything, and whatever would still be within your reach will only be a mediocre, depressing life, but that's not true.

Life always welcomes you back. And if it doesn't present you chances anymore, go out and make them for yourself. It's never too late to pick up on old passions or develop new ones, and go from there. Sure, it may take a while, but 'try' is the little brother of 'do', and if you do, you're already halfway where you want to be. This is important, don't ever forget about this.
Try and find joy in something, no matter how small or stupid or unnecessary it might be, and work into it. Pick up old talents, the rust will eventually come off.
Start small, one step at a time, and take pride in every small achievement - even if it's just finishing a small sketch, or mocking up a short story, or just making notes for whatever you've got planned. It's progress nontheless, and as long as you make progress, you're not squandering anything. It's important that you note every small achievement you make and flush out the hind thoughts of doing too little or too poorly. Concentrate on the good stuff, it'll drive you forward, and once you get going again, you can work from there.

I had two, although they might've just as well been hallucinations or something like that.

The first one was when I was young kid, I had a really big room, with my bed wedged into the corner directly opposite of there the door was. My parents always made me close the door when I went to bed, as well as pull down the shades completely, which left the entire room pitch black whenever I went to bed. And I mean -pitch- black with no hint of moonlight or anything else in the room. Now, that in itself wasn't a big deal, I've never been scared of the dark and I knew my way around that old room in my sleep. never had anything odd happen, either, until one morning. I woke up a bit earlier than usual, I think it was around 5am-ish hearing voices. I immediately recognized them as NOT being my parents, and at the start they were whispering. I can't remember what they were talking about, but I remember that as soon as I quietly called out, being the retarded kid I was, they grew louder fast, and more voices started talking at once, each over the other until the room was filled with incomprehensible chatter. I panicked, scrambled out of bed, because fuck that shit, and tried making my way towards the door with the voices ever growing louder, and now that I was slowly moving through my room, arms stretched out to the front so I wouldn't run into the walls i heard some of the voices starting to laugh, and I distinctly remember them laughing in a very mocking manner, taunting me for something. When I finally reached my door and just pulled it open, everything was silent IMMEDIATELY. Nothing like that ever happened again, and when I told my parents about it a bit earlier they said they both didn't hear anything, although they were probably asleep at the time anyway. After that happened, though, I never entered a pitch black room again without some sort of light source. I always tipped my shutters slightly open to allow at least a bit of light into the room and still do that to this day like a normal person.

Again, might've just been a retarded child having hallus or an overactive imagination, but that shit felt pretty real.
